description: A product's figure is the total units ordered across its order lines.

a.request: For each product (`product_id` on the order items), add up the units ordered (`product_quantity`, read as a whole number, ignoring missing values). Give each product a share: its units divided by the sum over all products. Then take the plain average of those shares across products. For the products whose share is strictly above that average, return a single unrounded row with: their combined units, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the overall average share.
a.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT product_id, SUM(CAST(product_quantity AS INTEGER)) AS units FROM Order_Items WHERE product_quantity IS NOT NULL GROUP BY product_id), s AS (SELECT product_id, units, CAST(units AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(units) FROM p) AS share FROM p), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(s.units) AS combined_units, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_excess FROM s, a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share

c.request: Looking at the order items, work out each product's (`product_id`) share of total order volume and the plain average of those shares across products. For the products whose share is strictly above that average, give me one unrounded row: their combined order volume, their average share, and how far, on average, their share sits above the average share. A product's figure is the total units ordered across its order lines.
c.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT product_id, SUM(CAST(product_quantity AS REAL)) AS units FROM Order_Items GROUP BY product_id), s AS (SELECT product_id, units, units / (SELECT SUM(units) FROM p) AS share FROM p), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(s.units) AS combined_order_volume, AVG(s.share) AS average_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS average_excess_over_average_share FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share

b.request: Compute each product's total units ordered (sum of `product_quantity` across its `Order_Items` lines) as a share of the total units ordered across all products, take the plain average of those per-product shares, then for products whose share is strictly above that average, return one unrounded row with the sum of their total units ordered, the average of their shares, and the average of (their share minus the average share)
b.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT product_id, SUM(CAST(product_quantity AS REAL)) AS units FROM Order_Items GROUP BY product_id), s AS (SELECT product_id, units, units / (SELECT SUM(units) FROM t) AS share FROM t), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(s.units) AS total_units_ordered, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_share_minus_overall_avg FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share

d.request: Looking at the order items, where each product's (`product_id`) volume is the total units ordered across its order lines, work out each product's share of total order volume and the plain average of those shares across products. For the products whose share is strictly above that average, give me one unrounded row containing their combined order volume, their average share, and how far, on average, their share sits above the average share.
d.sql: WITH vol AS (SELECT product_id, SUM(CAST(product_quantity AS REAL)) AS volume FROM Order_Items GROUP BY product_id), shares AS (SELECT product_id, volume, volume * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(volume) FROM vol) AS share FROM vol), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_s FROM shares) SELECT SUM(s.volume) AS combined_order_volume, AVG(s.share) AS average_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_s) AS average_excess_over_average_share FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_s
